description: Between 1 January and 30 September 2025, Israeli authorities demolished 1,288 Palestinian structures in the West Bank including East Jerusalem for lack of permits - an average of 4.7 per day, against 929 (3.4/day) in the same period of 2024. 2024's full-year figure was 1,768.
energy_note: Nearly five buildings a day, every day.

description: Those 2025 demolitions displaced 1,414 people and affected 38,017 others - the second figure being wells, sheds, classrooms, clinics, solar panels and access roads that served far more people than lived in them.
energy_note: Fourteen hundred homeless, thirty-eight thousand worse off.

aspect: The backlog is enormous and deliberate
description: The Civil Administration issued over 14,000 demolition orders against Palestinian-owned structures in Area C between 1988 and 2014. An outstanding order is a permanent conditional threat; the uncertainty is itself the instrument.
energy_note: Fourteen thousand houses waiting to hear.

aspect: You may be billed for your own demolition
description: Where authorities carry out the demolition, the costs of the operation can be charged to the owner. Families sometimes demolish their own homes to avoid the fee - and to avoid the bulldozer damaging the neighbours'.
money_note: Demolition costs charged to the owner.
energy_note: Taking down your own house to get the discount.

description: The first structure went in 2019. They rebuilt in tin and tarpaulin because concrete attracts attention. In 2024 that went too. The third is deliberately temporary - no foundations, nothing that reads as permanent - which also means no insulation, and the children are ill every winter.
energy_note: Building worse on purpose, so it hurts less to lose.

aspect: The right to challenge is narrowing
description: OCHA titled its 2025 reporting on this a peak in demolitions 'amidst increasing denial of the right to justice' - the review routes are closing at the same time as the demolitions accelerate.
energy_note: More demolitions, fewer ways to object.
